## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhīmasenajātaka* (Ja 80) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. The frame story recounts that the Buddha delivered the tale while residing at Jetavana, occasioned by a boastful monk who continually deceived his fellow brethren by bragging of his noble descent, royal lineage, and immense family wealth [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. In the tale of the past, the Bodhisatta goes into combat mounted on an elephant with a companion named Bhīmasena; upon hearing the battle drums, Bhīmasena is overwhelmed with terror and fouls the elephant's back, prompting the Bodhisatta to rebuke his cowardice with the opening verse *Yan te pavikatthitaṁ pure* ("You vaunted your prowess before..."), contrasting his previous boasts with his present disgrace [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877].

In his comparative study of Pali narrative literature, Eugene W. Burlingame associates the *Bhīmasena* story of the Jātaka collection with the narrative of *Tissa dahara* in the *Dhammapada* commentary (*Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*) [Burlingame 1921].

Neither SuttaCentral nor the DharmaNexus database identifies any curated or automated text reuse for Ja 80 within the Pali canon or among cross-language corpora in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral registers four modern translations of the tale across four languages [SuttaCentral].
